abstraction_fitness.description: TypeScript abstraction fitness: type and interface layers should improve safety and design clarity, not add ceremony or pass-through indirection.
look_for: Functions/components that only forward props or args without behavior, validation, or translation
Interfaces/types with one implementation and no polymorphic usage pressure
Large option objects passed through multiple layers with only a small subset used locally
Generic helper abstractions with one concrete type usage in practice
Cross-feature chains of wrappers that pass data unchanged between controller/service/helper layers
Widespread one-implementation interface ecosystems that add naming ceremony without substitution value
skip: React/Next.js framework composition patterns required by routing or lifecycle boundaries
Wrappers that intentionally add auth, telemetry, caching, feature flags, or retries
Public API typing shells that isolate external SDK volatility
Intentional barrel/facade exports that define stable package entry points

type_safety.description: TypeScript types that match runtime behavior, with escape hatches rare and justified
look_for: `any` (explicit, or implicit from `JSON.parse`, untyped imports or `catch` variables) flowing into typed code without narrowing
`as` casts asserting a shape nothing checks, `as unknown as T` double casts, and `!` on values that can really be undefined
External data (fetch responses, `JSON.parse`, `process.env`, request bodies) typed by annotation instead of validated at the boundary (zod, valibot, a type guard)
`@ts-ignore` or `@ts-expect-error` with no reason, or hiding a real bug
Unions handled without an exhaustive `never` check, or string literals compared where a union or enum type already exists
Loose types where a precise one exists: `object`, `Function`, `{}`, `Record<string, any>`, or `string` for a known set of values
Exported functions whose return type is inferred from a complex body, so an internal change silently changes the public API
skip: `any` confined to one interop module wrapping an untyped library
Casts right after a runtime check the compiler can't follow

dependency_health.description: package.json dependencies that are used, declared where they are imported, and not duplicated
look_for: Two libraries for one job (axios + a fetch wrapper, moment + dayjs/date-fns, lodash + native methods, jest + vitest)
Heavy runtime dependencies for light use (lodash for one helper, a date library for one format call)
Imports of packages the importing package's package.json doesn't declare, working only through hoisting
Runtime code importing `devDependencies`, or build and test tools listed in `dependencies`
In a monorepo, one dependency at different versions across packages, or workspace packages imported by relative path instead of by name
Deep imports into another package's internals (`pkg/dist/...`, `pkg/src/...`) instead of its public entry
skip: Peer dependencies a framework or plugin requires
Polyfills and `@types/*` packages kept for supported runtimes

test_strategy.description: Tests that cover the critical paths and assert behavior, not implementation
look_for: Critical modules (many importers, request handlers, data access) with no tests, or below target in the coverage report
`vi.mock`/`jest.mock` of the module's own internals, so tests assert call sequences instead of results
Snapshots (`toMatchSnapshot`, inline snapshots) as the main assertion for logic rather than rendered output
Async tests that neither await nor return the promise, and real timers where fake timers belong
Public generic or overloaded APIs with no type-level tests (`expectTypeOf`, `tsd`, `*.test-d.ts`)
React components tested through state or instance internals instead of Testing Library queries
Only unit tests: nothing runs a route, CLI or package entry point end to end
skip: Types-only, constants and barrel index files
Thin framework glue (route files that only wire a handler, config files)

system_prompt_append: TypeScript anchor checks: prop-drilling wrappers, single-implementation interfaces, generic surfaces used in only one concrete path, and recurring wrapper chains across feature boundaries.
